metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

brief.text:
The lead this morning is a change in how ships are being attacked. Trade press reports a tanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after explosives were attached to its hull, described as a new method of attack against commercial shipping, and separately a Greek container ship was sunk by naval drones off Bulgaria in the latest of several strikes in the western Black Sea. For anyone fixing ships, this is about where owners will agree to trade and at what war-risk premium, not just about cargo demand. It sits alongside tanker earnings that are extraordinary by any standard: the VLCC run from the Arabian Gulf to China (a very large crude carrier, roughly two million barrels) shows a time charter equivalent, or daily profit after voyage costs, of 1,287,851 USD/day, with Suezmax West Africa to UK Continent at 406,769 and Aframax North Sea to UK Continent at 481,500.

On prices, Brent crude fell 5.02 to 123.10 USD/bbl, down 3.9%, while WTI slipped only 1.88 to 103.37, leaving the Brent–WTI spread at 19.73 USD/bbl. The data here does not show why crude fell, and I would not tie it to any single headline. Henry Hub gas rose 9.5% to 2.76 USD/mmBtu; again, no explanation appears in today's data. Bunkers were mixed: VLSFO, the main fuel ships burn, was 1,002.00 USD/t in Singapore (+1.50), 778.00 in Rotterdam (+8.00), 984.00 in Fujairah (-5.50) and 837.50 in Houston (-4.50). The Baltic Dry Index, a composite of dry bulk freight rates, rose 60 points to 2,712, with the Capesize 5TC (big ore and coal ships) at 30,292 USD/day. Gasoline is stale, and coal API2, gasoil and the diesel crack have no data today.

Running stories: the Ras Tanura strike damage and the US Iran blockade warnings with a 125-vessel blacklist are unchanged today, with no fresh headline. Chokepoint transits had no new counts, but one report says Gulf oil producers are assembling nearly 230 tankers to keep exports moving through Hormuz amid owner reluctance. The Russian diesel trade developed: US energy importers are reported to be pushing back politically against the deal. Boluda's Samskip takeover is now described as a 32-vessel network across 28 countries.

Watch two things: further attack reports in Hormuz and the Black Sea, which drive war-risk cost and routing; and Fujairah congestion, where 265 dry bulk vessels were waiting as of 28 October.

storylines.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
storylines.what: A tanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after explosives were attached to its hull, reported as a new method of attack against commercial shipping, with multiple incidents reported. Gulf oil producers are said to be assembling nearly 230 tankers to keep crude moving through the strait amid owner reluctance.
storylines.why_it_matters: Limpet-style attacks on hulls raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for ships transiting Hormuz, shrinking the pool of owners willing to lift Arabian Gulf cargoes and feeding into already extreme VLCC and Suezmax earnings.
storylines.latest: First report of explosives attached to a tanker hull in Hormuz, and a report that Gulf producers are building a near-230 tanker fleet to maintain exports.

storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea this month that have raised concerns about a widening conflict.
storylines.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure in the Black Sea threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.

storylines.title: Houthi strike damage at Ras Tanura
storylines.what: Satellite imagery has confirmed that a Houthi missile strike on the Saudi oil export hub of Ras Tanura hit a critical component of the complex.
storylines.why_it_matters: Ras Tanura is a major crude loading point; damage there affects crude availability and risk premiums for tankers loading in the Arabian Gulf, and sits alongside exceptionally high VLCC earnings.

storylines.title: US Iran blockade warnings and vessel blacklist
storylines.what: US forces have reiterated blockade warnings to shipping, with the PGSA blacklist expanding to 125 vessels, alongside a piracy warning for the Gulf of Aden.
storylines.why_it_matters: A growing blacklist shrinks the compliant tanker pool and raises war-risk and routing costs through Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab, which feeds directly into crude and product tanker earnings.

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Hormuz recorded six VLCC transits on Oct 25, the most since Oct 17, while Bab al-Mandab recorded one VLCC on each of Oct 24 and Oct 25. Separately, vessel waiting remains elevated across the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, with 265 dry bulk vessels waiting as of 28 October and Fujairah holding 28% of them.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times are a direct read on whether ships are routing through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
storylines.latest: Gulf congestion reported elevated with 265 dry bulk vessels waiting as of 28 October; Fujairah takes 28%. No new transit counts today.

storylines.title: Russian diesel returning across the Atlantic
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market is said to be creating a new trade, but it has run into political opposition, with pushback now reported to be gaining traction among US energy importers.
storylines.why_it_matters: A reopened Atlantic diesel route would reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns, but political and legal resistance leaves the trade uncertain.
storylines.latest: Pushback against Russian diesel reported to be gaining traction with US energy importers.
